summary.headline: Steelcast FY26 revenue rose 13.33% to ₹423.17 crore and PAT 20.31% to ₹86.86 crore; management guides 20%+ volume growth for FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached ₹423.17 crore (up 13.33% YoY), EBITDA ₹129.64 crore (margin 30.64%, up 104 bps) and PAT ₹86.86 crore (up 20.31%). Q4FY26 revenue of ₹112.43 crore rose 15.43% QoQ, with EBITDA ₹34.25 crore and PAT ₹23.18 crore, but management acknowledged volumes and revenue were below the prior-year quarter. Margin pressure in Q4 came from higher maintenance, power and energy costs (fuel prices), and export-related provisions, with raw material costs up about 10% since March 1. Management said the capacity expansion decision will be taken by end-July 2026 instead of December 2026, citing stronger customer indications.

financial_highlights.change: +20.31% YoY from ₹72.20 crore; margin +119 bps from 19.34%

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports contributed over 60% of FY26 revenue and outperformed domestic business in both the quarter and the full year; North America and developed markets were steady, with new engagement from global OEMs.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic business grew sequentially in Q4FY26 but trailed exports; management did not give a separate domestic revenue figure.

segments.name: Ground engaging tools (GET)
segments.commentary: GET was 1.1% of FY26 sales; management plans to take it to 3.8% in FY27 from existing customers.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Management has shifted focus away from defence; repeat overseas orders for compact-vehicle parts (prototypes approved, awaiting serial supply) could yield ₹15-18 crore in sales if they materialise.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 20%+ volume growth in FY27 and sees 20%+ cumulative annual growth through FY29; the PAT aspiration is more than ₹100 crore in FY27 (described as an aspiration, not guidance).
Sustainable EBITDA margin of 25-26% is seen as realistic over the longer term, though levels nearer 30% may occur at times.
Raw material costs rose about 10% from March 1; price pass-through of 4-5% expected, with partial compensation from April 1 and the balance from July 1. Management expects to be largely covered.
Aspiration to double sales by FY29 versus FY26 using present capacity (cited as ~₹860 crore in FY29).
2.4 MW hybrid power project due for commissioning by June 2026, with expected annual savings of ~₹3.6 crore.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion decision to be taken by end-July 2026 (previously contemplated by December 2026); exact size and numbers to be shared then, and management said it is about halfway through the exercise.
Current-year capacity utilisation expected at about 63-64%; management no longer plans to wait for 75% utilisation before expanding.
Over 50 new parts are at various development stages; new parts are moving into serial supply, which management says is significantly accelerating in the last 4-6 weeks.
Part weight range within existing capability is 5 kg to 2,500 kg.
Order book for Q1FY27 is about ₹130-135 crore as of 1 April, with a typical cycle of 110-120 days.
demand_pricing: Management says realisations are steady; sales price variation formulas with all customers allow cost increases to be passed through automatically (and cost decreases passed back).

Exports are supported by supply-chain diversification (China+1) and steady North American demand; some serial orders from overseas are delayed by the Iran-US conflict, with management expecting them in one to two quarters.
Management sees no significant data-centre demand for steel castings.

Target end markets are mining, earthmoving, construction, locomotives, railroad and ground engaging tools. Railroad development has faced unresolved challenges; competition is more favourable in the other segments.
Working capital cycles are generally 75-110 days; the blended receivables are about 90-95 days per an analyst's reading of the company's figures.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic demand rise from data-centre capex, and will defence exports expand to new geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said data centres need practically no steel castings, so no meaningful demand uplift is expected. Overseas defence parts are approved and await serial orders, expected within one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex now proceed before 75% utilisation, given demand visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; current utilisation is about 63-64%, and the company will decide on expansion by end-July 2026 instead of December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of cost increases and pass-through on realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs rose about 10%, with a 4-5% sales price impact; partial compensation applied from April 1 and the rest from July 1. Realisations remain steady under variation formulas.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin outlook 25-26% or 28-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25-26% is the more realistic sustainable EBITDA margin over the longer term, though levels near 30% can occur at times.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution expected from GET in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: GET was 1.1% of FY26 sales; the company plans 3.8% in FY27 from existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company going to disclose a more detailed revenue breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed to add sector-wise and granular export breakdowns from Q1FY27.

risks_watch: Q4FY26 showed margin pressure from maintenance, power and fuel costs; the pass-through timing (July 1 balance) and rupee depreciation will determine the Q1FY27 margin.
Railroad development problems remain unresolved, and management did not quantify the impact.
Delays in overseas serial orders linked to the Iran-US conflict; the defence order sizing (₹15-18 crore) depends on conversion.
Capacity expansion decision and sizing due end-July 2026; capex project cost and timeline not yet disclosed.
Management clarified the PAT ₹100 crore goal is an aspiration with no firm date, and the 20% growth refers to volume, not PAT; investors should not read it as PAT guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FY27 growth ambition, but cautious on near-term margins, which management said will be pressured by fuel and raw material costs. Management was evasive on capex size, project cost and Q4 year-on-year decline, deferring to annual comparisons and the July decision date.

sustained EBITDA margins of 25%, 26% is a reasonable thing to expect going forward.
So there is no really effect on realizations.

adds.what: 2.4 MW hybrid power project (energy, not production capacity)

growth.why: Management targets 20%+ volume growth in FY27 and 20%+ annually through FY29, backed by a Q1FY27 order book of about ₹130-135 crore (110-120 day cycle), 50+ new parts moving to serial supply, and 4-5% price pass-through; capacity expansion decision is deferred to end-July 2026 with no size or timing yet, so backing is partial.
